correctness.rationale: For every n>=7, classified maximal cliques using unique distance-two column pairs and intersections of radius-one neighborhoods in C_5, listed n+5n+5n maximal facets, and checked exactly six free-face pairs for each B and two for each C. This proves a 40n-step simplicial collapse to a torus triangulation with n meridian-filling four-simplices. A standard cofibration gluing argument replaces those contractible pieces with n meridian disks, and cellular cancellation of one primitive meridian yields S^1 wedge n S^2. The full vector follows from counting target simplices and reversing 40n pairs. The actual included checker separately enumerated all radius-two cliques and verified face equality/free pairs for n=7..14 and computed mod-two homology for n=7..10; finite checks do not replace the uniform argument.

originality.rationale: The exact pentagonal rectangular radius-two homotopy type with all n>=7 is not stated or implied by the strongest full texts examined. The 2025 square-grid source fixes both periods equal; its n=5,k=2 result is only the 5-by-5 boundary. The closest published rectangular widths are four-cycles (different homotopy degree), complete-graph fibers (different shortest-path metric), and twist-period families m,n>=7 (different quotient geometry). Multiple actual semantic searches for aliases, exact homotopy formula, and parameter-specialization competitors returned these but no dominating theorem. Acknowledged risk: prior results outside the inspected and indexed corpus. The final exact-formula search also yielded a circular-ladder Čech theorem with the same wedge ranks, but full-text inspection confirmed distinct graphs and simplicial constructions, so it is not covering.
residual_risks: Semantic retrieval cannot rule out mathematically equivalent results not indexed or labeled unexpectedly; this does not erase the affirmative theorem-by-theorem implication comparisons.

value.rationale: The length-five toroidal factor is a mathematically natural boundary between the published four-cycle thin-cylinder class with n three-spheres and the equal large-square torus regime. It kills precisely one primitive meridian but generates n independent degree-two homology classes. Uniform free-face collapse and explicit CW decomposition explain the structural mechanism for all n>=7, beyond an isolated finite computation or routine parameter substitution. The full homotopy classification is a meaningful new rectangular-family benchmark for graph-metric Rips topology.
